request.state: We need resolve semantic registry representability without a global size policy. Judge each alternative on exact nonaliasing IDs, graceful all-client error handling, recoverable-error compatibility, no false completion, and the smallest justified implementation. ModuleId, SymbolId and ScopeId are u32 zero-based indexes into private resolver vectors; the last index u32::MAX is representable. Inspected private module/symbol/scope allocators currently cast vector.len() from usize to u32 before push, including several generated field/parameter/CRUD/preference insertion routes. IR only copies those resolver IDs. Public resolve_program accepts a mutable diagnostics vector and returns ResolveTables directly. The main check_program then runs dependent type/effect/example passes regardless ordinary errors and returns checked facts plus sorted diagnostics. Native CLI refuses erroneous results; low-level public tables remain caller-editable with documented diagnostic/shipping responsibility. Existing finite 100/1000/3000 real declaration graph controls qualify order/IDs/types/edges/cycles at those inputs; they do not allocate billions of IDs. Do not add a configurable resource cap, truncate/alias IDs, forge carriers, manufacture an ID sentinel, duplicate the resolver in test/count code, or run giant allocation probes. Capacity refusal must occur before invalid insertion and dependent analysis must not interpret failed resolution as complete.

resolver_admission.instructions: Which contract should be selected for the next bounded implementation? Treat output as advisory and retain uncertainty; do not infer unexecuted giant-input qualification.

criteria.fallible_abort: Use checked private ID allocation and propagate a capacity failure to one owning fallible resolver entrance. Retain the existing public entrance as a compatibility wrapper which adds the fatal diagnostic and returns empty tables on capacity failure; the main checker uses the fallible entrance and skips dependent passes on this failure, returning empty checked semantic collections with the original input association and error. Ordinary recoverable diagnostics continue as before. Adds explicit failure propagation and discards prefix tables; no invalid/truncated ID is published.
criteria.partial_abort: Use checked private allocation and stop resolution at capacity failure, retaining the valid prefix tables plus one fatal diagnostic and an explicit failed-status marker. The checker skips dependent passes unless the marker says full resolution completed. Public clients may inspect a prefix under the documented error boundary. Preserves available prefix data but adds a status/partial-table API contract and requires all users to distinguish it from completed facts; no guessed IDs or continued resolution after failure.
criteria.widen_ids: Widen module/symbol/scope identity types to usize or u64 across allocator/indexing/public carrier paths and their consumers. Keep original allocation order and exact indexes; coordinate external typed/API/serialization compatibility and explicit remaining finite machine limits. Removes this u32 ID boundary but changes the published identity domain and creates a larger migration. Source byte offsets and source identities retain their separate already-admitted u32 contracts.
